scope: New Zealand symbol manifest and current flagMeaning/adoption data, extended to obvious historical artwork contradictions
method: Read all 11 manifest records, render all 11 repository images with sharp, compare descriptions; nine declared image SHA-256 values all match bundled bytes. Read primary government/museum/PRADO evidence. Four incorrect strings confirmed in deployed 71e380b JS. No browser rendering certification.

records.design: The national flag of New Zealand, in the form adopted in 1903.
records.observation: Manifest/generated card/adoption table say 1903; official government history identifies 1902 statutory recognition and technical notice. General flagMeaning correctly says 1902. Appearance broadly agrees; SVG digital colours differ from Ministry approximate RGB equivalents, not adjudicated legally invalid.

records.design: The first New Zealand flag based on the Blue Ensign, defaced with the letters NZ.
records.description: Adopted by a warrant of Governor Sir George Grey published 10 January 1867, this flag set the red letters 'NZ', bordered white, on a British Blue Ensign — New Zealand's first officially devised colonial emblem, created after two government steamers were reprimanded by visiting Royal Navy ships in 1866 for flying a plain, unbadged Blue Ensign, in breach of Britain's 1865 Colonial Naval Defence Act. The letters were replaced in 1869 by the four-star Southern Cross device that, redrawn over the following decades, remains on New Zealand's flag today.
records.observation: Red NZ with white border on Blue Ensign agrees with government history; 1867-1869 maritime chronology supported. Specific 10 January warrant date not independently checked.

records.design: The Union Flag, which served as New Zealand’s flag from the Treaty of Waitangi until a distinct colonial ensign was granted.
records.description: The Union Flag superimposes the crosses of three patron saints: Saint George's red cross on white for England, Saint Andrew's white saltire on blue for Scotland, and Saint Patrick's red saltire on white for Ireland. Combined in its current form in 1801 to mark the union of Great Britain and Ireland, it represents the political union of the United Kingdom's constituent nations.
records.observation: End year 1867 conflates introduction of maritime ensign with replacement of onshore national/legal flag in 1902.

records.design: A banner of the New Zealand shield with the Queen’s personal cypher.
records.description: A banner of the New Zealand coat of arms' shield — the four stars of the Southern Cross, a ship for maritime trade, a fleece for farming, a wheat sheaf for agriculture and crossed hammers for mining, with two fern leaves (the native silver fern) beneath — defaced with a blue disc bearing a crowned gold letter 'E' within a garland of roses: Queen Elizabeth II's own royal cypher. Approved in 1962 for the Queen's use while in New Zealand as its head of state, the flag went out of use on her death in September 2022.
records.observation: No fern leaves beneath shield: rectangular banner of shield with crowned E/rose disc; description imports ferns from full arms. Complete historical period/current successor flag not certified.

records.design: A St George’s cross on white, with a second cross and four stars in the canton — chosen by 25 northern chiefs in 1834 so New Zealand-built ships could be registered.
records.description: Chosen by a gathering of Māori chiefs at Waitangi on 20 March 1834 — the design that won a vote among several submitted flags — the United Tribes flag combined a red St George's cross with a smaller blue-and-black-bordered cross bearing four white eight-pointed stars. It was adopted so New Zealand-built ships would not be seized for lacking a flag of registry, but its deeper significance was that Britain's recognition of it acknowledged Māori chiefs' mana and marked the first act of collective Māori nationhood, uniting previously separate tribes under one flag.
records.observation: Bundled canton cross is white-bordered; caption says black-bordered original. NZHistory distinguishes the approved white-border variant from original black-border design. 20 March 1834 and 25 chiefs supported; precise change-date not assigned.

records.design: A red ensign with four white stars representing the Southern Cross.
records.description: The four stars are the same Southern Cross constellation shown on the national flag, positioned to match the real stars Acrux, Mimosa, Gacrux and Delta Crucis as seen from New Zealand; the ensign was adopted in 1901 for merchant vessels and can also be flown on land for occasions of Māori significance.
records.observation: Red field, Union canton, four white stars and Maori-significance land use agree with Ministry. 1901 adoption and exact named-star placement not separately checked.

records.design: A shield of the Southern Cross, a fleece, a wheat sheaf, crossed hammers and three ships, borne by a European woman with the flag and a Māori rangatira with a taiaha, crowned by St Edward's Crown.
records.description: The shield reads the country's making: the four stars of the Southern Cross, a golden fleece for wool, a wheat sheaf for farming, crossed hammers for mining, and three ships down the centre for sea trade and the immigrant character of New Zealanders. The supporters embody its bicultural identity — a European woman holding the national flag and a Māori rangatira bearing a taiaha. St Edward's Crown marks the monarchy, and silver fern fronds flank the “New Zealand” scroll. Granted in 1911 and revised to the present form in 1956.
records.observation: Four stars, three ships, fleece, wheat, crossed hammers, European woman/NZ flag, Maori chief/taiaha, St Edward crown, 1911 grant and 1956 revision agree with Ministry. No pixel-exact blazon certification or verification of every interpretive gloss.

records.design: The cover of the New Zealand passport.
records.description: New Zealand's passport bears the national coat of arms: a shield showing the four stars of the Southern Cross, three ships for maritime trade, a fleece and a sheaf of wheat for farming, and crossed hammers for mining, crowned to mark the country's status as a constitutional monarchy. The shield is flanked by two supporters — a Māori rangatira (chief) holding a taiaha and a European woman holding the New Zealand flag — representing the country's two founding peoples, with fern branches, a native plant and a longstanding national emblem, framing the base.
records.observation: Bundled drawn cover is English-first with warm gold-coloured artwork. DIA 3 May 2021 announces Maori-first replacement and continued validity of older books; PRADO NZL-AO-04001 first issue 15 April 2021, silver foil on black. Exact older series/foil reproduction pending; do not label earlier books invalid.

records.design: A black upper field and red lower field divided by a white koru.
records.description: Designed by Hiraina Marsden in 1990 and recognised in 2009 as the national Māori flag, its colours follow the Māori creation account: black for Te Korekore, the realm of potential being; red for Te Whai Ao, the coming into being; and white for Te Ao Mārama, the world of light. The white koru — an unfurling fern frond — stands for renewal and hope, and the white also evokes Aotearoa, the “land of the long white cloud.”
records.observation: Current description credits only Hiraina Marsden in 1990. Official sources credit Hiraina Marsden, Jan Dobson Smith and Linda Munn in 1989; unveiling in 1990. Cabinet recognition 14 Dec 2009 as preferred national Maori flag, not statutory official national flag. Existing three-realm colour meanings agree with Ministry.

records.design: The crest of the New Zealand men's national football team — a black silver fern frond.
records.description: The silver fern has marked New Zealand sporting teams since the 1888–89 New Zealand Native rugby team's tour of Britain, and was carried by New Zealand's expeditionary forces in both World Wars — it is engraved on the Commonwealth war graves of fallen New Zealand soldiers. It is shared today across the country's national teams, including the women's football side, the Football Ferns.
records.observation: Outlined fern. Sports history, logo variant/date and rights not independently checked.

records.design: The New Zealand Olympic Committee's mark: a silver fern frond, a national symbol of New Zealand, above the words “NEW ZEALAND OLYMPIC COMMITTEE” and the Olympic rings.
records.observation: Fern over NEW ZEALAND OLYMPIC COMMITTEE and rings; design line broadly matches. Participation/medal counts, foundation date and brand currentness unverified.
